source: All-In Podcast — GPT-5 underwhelms, AI TAM/ROIC/energy, China's advantage, tariffs, Nvidia chip smuggling, Apple buybacks and AI strategy
summary: Apple is dramatically underperforming in AI and has wasted capital on buybacks that could have funded competitive AI infrastructure, representing a strategic failure.
summary_extended: Baker expresses strong conviction that Apple has committed a serious strategic failure by dramatically underinvesting in AI while simultaneously over-allocating capital to share buybacks. He argues Apple could have spent $200 billion less on buybacks and instead invested in data center infrastructure to become a genuine AI competitor, but instead has produced AI products he describes as 'terrible' from a user perspective, with Siri having actually regressed in quality. Baker says he is 'shocked' and 'baffled' by Apple's inaction and 'inaptitude' in AI, going so far as to say it 'almost feels like they're trying to lose.' While he stops short of an explicit sell recommendation, the thesis frames Apple's capital allocation decisions as a medium-term strategic liability that leaves the company poorly positioned in the AI era relative to peers who have invested aggressively in infrastructure.
